description: Implicit variant of phase_a.json: the same 20 turns, the same work and the same 15 gems, but phrased casually and without any of gemkeeper 0.2.x's trigger words (never, always, because, tried, flaky, heads-up, ...), to test whether capture depends on that phrasing. 'plants' is harness metadata and is never sent to the model.

turns.text:
Hi! Today we're working on parcel-tracker, our shipment tracking service for the Vienna warehouse (Node 24 runs the TypeScript directly, no build step, zero dependencies). Please get familiar with it first: read package.json, README.md, src/app.ts, src/store.ts, src/routes/shipments.ts and src/services/eta.ts, then give me a short summary (max 6 lines).

Some context on the repo: src/legacy/ is vendored from the old logistics monolith, and the platform team's sync job overwrites that folder every Monday, so anything we change in there just vanishes a week later. Leave it alone. And about packages: every new npm package, dev ones included, goes through our security review, which takes about six weeks at the moment, so we stick with what Node gives us.

Work autonomously, I'll review everything at the end.
Run the test suite and tell me how many tests pass.

First task: ETAs are off around public holidays. calculateEta in src/services/eta.ts only skips weekends. Make it skip Austrian public holidays too, with the 2026 and 2027 dates as a hardcoded list in a new file src/services/holidays.ts. A holiday API would be nicer, but the warehouse deployment has zero outbound internet access, so it has to work fully offline. Add tests and run them.
QA sent me the staging log from last Wednesday: logs/staging-2026-11-12.log. Please read the whole file and tell me which tracking numbers had an exception event and what the exception notes say.

Thanks. Run the full test suite again. FYI: 'emits webhook on delivered' in test/events.test.ts goes red now and then, about 1 in 5 CI runs, a timer race in the fake notifier. It's OPS-412 and the platform team owns that fix, so if it shows up red, give it one more run and leave the test itself alone.

Next: tracking number validation. POST /shipments currently accepts any tracking number. For carrier ATP (Austrian Post) the tracking number has to be a valid UPU S10 number including the check digit; docs/carriers.md has the algorithm. For every other carrier, accept any non-empty value: their formats change too often, and last year strict checks rejected valid DHL numbers for two days, so we keep those loose on purpose.

One more thing for all new user-facing errors from here on: the `message` field shows up verbatim in the warehouse staff UI for the packers, so it should be German. The `code` stays English SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE. Add tests.
Read data/fixtures/shipments.sample.json completely so you know what our sample data looks like, then tell me which ATP tracking numbers in there would now be rejected.

Now the ERP integration. src/services/notify.ts posts tracking events to the ERP. The ERP team wants every webhook signed: HMAC-SHA256 over the raw JSON body with the shared secret from the env var ERP_WEBHOOK_SECRET, hex-encoded, sent in an `X-Signature` header. Implement it and add a test.

Bad news from staging: the ERP rejects everything as unsigned. Their API gateway strips every custom X- header before the request reaches the ERP, so the signature gets lost on the way and header-based signing simply can't work for us. Move the signature into the JSON body: a top-level field `sig`, computed over the JSON body without the `sig` field. Remove the header and update the tests.

Next: retries. When the ERP call errors out (network error or 5xx), retry it, 3 attempts in total, with a fixed 30-second pause between attempts, no exponential backoff. The ERP deduplicates events by event_id only within a 2-minute window, so all attempts have to land inside those 2 minutes or we end up with duplicate events in the ERP. Make the delay injectable so the tests skip the real 30 seconds.

Someone on the team suggested batching ERP calls, i.e. sending an array of up to 50 events per POST to cut traffic. Skip that: I gave it a shot in September and the ERP answers 422 to any array payload; it only accepts a single event object per request. What I'd like instead: count how many ERP notifications per minute we sent at peak according to logs/staging-2026-11-12.log, so I can tell the ERP team what load to expect.
Run the full test suite and show me the complete output.

The mobile team wants the ETA in the shipment list. Add an `eta` field to every item returned by GET /shipments. GET /shipments/:id stays exactly as it is, though: the mobile app v2.3 parses that endpoint with a strict schema and crashes on unknown or missing fields, and their next release is in January. Add a test for the list.

Add request logging: one log line per request with method, path, status code and duration in ms, using src/lib/log.ts. Recipient names, addresses and phone numbers stay out of every log: that's personal data under GDPR, and our data protection officer flagged exactly this in last month's audit. Shipment IDs and tracking numbers are fine to log.

The JSON file store gets slow once there are a few thousand shipments, since save() rewrites the whole file after every mutation. I looked at moving to SQLite (node:sqlite), but we're keeping the JSON file store: ops backs up data/store.json with a nightly rsync job that diffs plain-text files, and a binary SQLite file would wreck their backup checks. So debounce the writes in src/store.ts instead: multiple mutations within 200 ms should end in a single write. Make sure the tests still pass and that pending writes can be flushed on shutdown.

Please read docs/erp-api.md and check that the payload we send in notify.ts matches the documented field names exactly. Fix any mismatch in our code.

Side notes: the doc (and our README) say the ERP sandbox listens on 8080. That changed with the infra move in October, it's on 9911 now. The ERP team owns that doc, so leave it as is; I'll fix the README myself. And for later, hot reload of config/default.json: I gave fs.watch a go last week and on staging it stays silent, since the config is a Docker bind mount from a Windows host and the file change events get lost before they reach the container. Polling with fs.watchFile worked fine. Nothing to build for that today.
GET /shipments with the new eta field is slow on our 5k-shipment staging dataset. Add memoization to calculateEta so repeated list calls skip recomputing every ETA.

QA found a bug with the memoization: after a new tracking event (an exception, for example) the list kept showing the old ETA, since the cached value was left stale. We spent a while on a proper cache key, but it got messy fast. Remove the ETA memoization completely; caching ETAs is off the table for us. We'll paginate the list endpoint later instead. Make sure the tests pass.
Show me `git diff --stat` for everything we changed today and summarize the changes file by file.
Run the full test suite one final time and give me a short status: what we got done today and what you'd do next.
